subject: MedSys data handling: proposed 0-retention pilot & next steps
messages:
From: jasmine.liu@redwood.ai
To: tom.reynolds@medsys.io, asha@medsys.io
Cc: security@medsys.io
Date: 2026-03-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MedSys data handling: proposed 0-retention pilot & next steps

Tom / Asha — thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

Key takeaways from discovery:
- Primary ask: avoid persisting any request/response logs that contain PHI (we heard the ask described as “0-retention for PHI routes”).
- Secondary: data residency — production inference must run in us-east-1 and offer contractual residency guarantees.
- Observability: MedSys requires some audit trail but wants the ability to opt routes out of logging for sensitive flows.

Options we discussed (high-level):
1) Sensitive mode (0-retention) — no request/response logs persisted for selected API routes; no KV/prefix caching for those routes.
2) Short window logs — keep logs for configurable short windows (7/30/90 days) for non-PHI routes.
3) Token redaction + selective telemetry — keep anonymized metrics for billing/latency only.

Immediate asks / next steps:
- Can you confirm which endpoints you want in Sensitive mode vs Short-window? (Asha + security team)
- We’ll scope a pilot: 30-day pilot where up to 2 routes are put in Sensitive mode. We’ll surface trade-offs in debugability and SLA (throughput may be slightly reduced).
- I’ve attached a short data sample schema and our SOC2 snippet for quick review.

Attachments: redwood-data-sample-schema.csv; SOC2-snip.pdf

If that all sounds right I’ll loop in Rishi for the pricing delta and bring Lauren in for any escalation. Proposed pilot kickoff: next Tue (25th) — are you available?

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0198
Redwood Inference
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@medsys.io>
To: jasmine.liu@redwood.ai, asha@medsys.io
Cc: security@medsys.io
Date: 2026-03-18T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MedSys data handling: proposed 0-retention pilot & next steps

Thanks, Jasmine — clear summary. A few clarifications from the security team:

- When you say "no request/response logs persisted", do you still keep transient buffers (in memory) for inference caching? We need assurance that nothing is written to disk or long-lived stores.
- We will need an auditable record that the Sensitive mode was enabled/disabled (who toggled it and when). Full payloads for toggled routes must not be retained.
- Data residency: all model inference must occur in us-east-1 (we cannot accept routing to other regions).

We’re also considering a carve-out where certain PII-free routes can have a 7-day log window for troubleshooting. For routes ingesting PHI, we want 0-retention and no KV cache.

Attaching the team’s data classification for your reference.

On the pilot timing — Tue 25th works for a short kickoff (we can do 30–45 minutes). If you can send a short SOW or amendment that outlines the Sensitive mode behaviors and the audit toggles we can start the internal approval.

Thanks — Tom
Tom Reynolds
Director of Platform Security, MedSys Health
Tom.Reynolds@medsys.io
Attachment: MedSys-data-classification.xlsx

Date: 2026-03-18T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: MedSys data handling: proposed 0-retention pilot & next steps

Forwarding Tom’s notes — key asks are: 0-retention for PHI routes (no disk persistence, no KV cache), region lock to us-east-1, and an audit trail for toggles (not payloads).

Rishi — can you run high-level pricing delta for a Sensitive mode (0-retention) per-month premium? Think about both hosted and Dedicated options — they may prefer hosted with strict region pinning for simplicity. Also include cost impact if we disable prefix caching for those routes (expected token cost increase).

Vanessa / Lauren — recommended sales play: offer a 30-day pilot with 2 routes in Sensitive mode, provide an SA amendment (DocuSign) that describes the technical controls, and include limited support hours during pilot.

I’ll draft the amendment once we have the pricing and legal bullet points.

-JL
From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
To: jasmine.liu@redwood.ai, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-03-18T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: MedSys data handling: proposed 0-retention pilot & next steps

Quick cost readout (high level):
- Sensitive mode (0-retention, no KV/prefix cache): ~+18–25% per-token unit cost because we lose cache savings and pay extra for in-memory-only secure paths.
- Region lock (us-east-1 enforcement): no direct premium if hosted capacity available; if Dedicated required, add Dedicated capacity baseline (~$Xk/mo) depending on throughput.
- Short-window logs (7 days): negligible tier change; main cost is storage at scale.

Recommendation: Pilot pricing — set a temporary +20% per-token surcharge for Sensitive routes for the pilot. Include a clause that production pricing will be revisited after pilot (we’ll provide precise forecast after we instrument with sample telemetry).

I attached a simple cost delta CSV with assumptions. I’ll sync with Product on implementation notes around disabling prefix caching safely.

- Rishi
Attachment: retention-cost-delta.csv

Subject: Re: MedSys data handling: proposed 0-retention pilot & next steps

Tom / Asha — thanks for the quick turnaround and for the classification doc. We can support the MedSys requirements and here’s the concrete proposal: 

1) Pilot scope and controls
- Pilot: 30 days, start date TBD (we suggested Mar 25).
- Two routes designated as "Sensitive mode": no request/response logs persisted, no KV/prefix caching, inference executed in us-east-1 only.
- Toggling audit: we will record toggle events (who/when) but will not store payloads. Audit records will include route id, toggle timestamp, and actor identity.

2) Trade-offs / caveats
- Debugging is limited for Sensitive routes — we will not have full payload logs for post-mortem. We will offer a secure debug flow where MedSys can submit a captured request (with patient consent/PII redaction) for manual debug under an agreed process.
- SLA: small potential latency variance when caching is disabled; Rishi flagged ~20% per-token cost uplift.

3) Next steps & asks from MedSys
- Please confirm the two route ids you want in Sensitive mode.
- Legal: sign an SA amendment (DocuSign link below) to capture the data control commitments for the pilot.
- Security questionnaire: please send your standard form and we’ll respond within 3 business days.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/templates/MedSys-SA-amendment
HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/88431

If that looks good I’ll slot the kickoff for Tue 2026-03-25 at 09:00 PT and route the amendment to your legal. Appreciate the quick help from your team.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
